name: ufsprobe
description: The FILESYSTEM, asserted on the machine against an independent implementation of its format: the 2.11BSD superblock (UFS 1.10a) and the block and inode allocators (1.10b).  IT RUNS FROM ufs.mod, its own module since apple/fgx#169, and every buffer-cache call it makes CROSSES A BANK BOUNDARY -- bread, getblk, bwrite and brelse are resolved out of vfs.mod's VT_VFSCORE table at load time and reached through the shims in src/modules/ufs/vfs_import.s.  That makes this test the only coverage the module-to-module seam has: a wrong argument frame or a missed DBR switch in a shim shows up here as a specific case number, because the assertions below are exact values rather than 'it did not crash'.  It also still asserts the split gate it was created for at 1.10b.  UFS 1.10c ADDED bmap, and with it a real multi-level file: the ufsscratch rule now runs `fgxfs mkfile /big --blocks 300` after mkfs, so the volume carries a file whose blocks reach through the four direct addresses, a single indirect and into a double indirect -- 300 being the smallest round size that reaches the second level.  The triple indirect starts at logical block 65796, a 64 MB file on a 4 MB disk, so that level is covered by a chain the probe builds by hand in three blocks nothing else touches, with a DIFFERENT index at each level so a walk using the wrong shift lands on a zero entry rather than accidentally agreeing.  MUTATION-VERIFIED at 1.10c, five arms: indexing the wrong indirect slot, reading indirect entries little-endian, an off-by-one in the index mask, and returning 2.11BSD's 0 for a hole instead of Reno's -1 all go red (605, 605, 605, 612); and zeroing the MIDDLE level of the synthetic chain gives 624, which is what proves the triple walk reads all three blocks.  WHAT MAKES A GREEN HERE MEAN ANYTHING is that every expected value comes from tools/fgxfs.py, a host implementation of the same format that shares no source with this kernel: disk/ufsscratch.po is built by `fgxfs mkfs --size 4096` at build time, and the probe asserts the numbers that tool put there.  Two implementations agreeing about a format is the claim goal 2 of the campaign rests on -- an FGX volume a PDP-11 will mount; one implementation agreeing with itself would be worth nothing.  THE CASE THAT CARRIES THE WEIGHT IS THE REFILL.  The superblock caches exactly 29 block addresses on this volume; the 29th allocation empties the cache and the address it returns, block 93, IS the chain block holding the next fifty.  So allocations 30 onward (95, 97, 99, 100) can only be right if the kernel read block 93 off the disk and decoded it out of PDP-11 byte order, high word first -- those numbers exist nowhere but on the platter.  It also covers: the encode direction pinned by BYTES rather than by a round trip (a half-swap written backwards round-trips perfectly and produces a volume no PDP-11 can read); badblock's refusals, re-checking the counts afterwards because a refusal that had already pushed the address would still return EINVAL and look correct; the spill, verified with a RAW kc_blkio read so the oracle is the layer below; ialloc's i-list scan, which mkfs forces by leaving fs_ninode at 0, and whose first inode is 103 rather than 4 because the scan fills the cache ascending and ialloc pops from the top; ifree's two arms that throw the number away but must not lose the count; and every ENOSPC refusal.  IT WRITES AND IT PUTS THE SUPERBLOCK BACK, including on failure -- the image is handed to MAME by path with no per-run copy, and ninja will not rebuild an output newer than its inputs, so a superblock left modified would fail the next boot's case 403 and keep failing.  UFS 1.8a ADDED THE MOUNT, which is the first time this tree attaches a filesystem to anything: cases 700-715 build a struct mount with a struct ufsmount hanging off it, check the private data is wired both ways, and assert the df numbers -- 4030 blocks, 3725 free, 1024 inodes, 1020 free -- against what fgxfs reports for the same volume.  The mapping is 2.11BSD's statfs1 and not Reno's, whose cylinder-group summary a 2.11BSD volume does not have, so f_bavail equals f_bfree where FFS would subtract a minfree reserve.  TWO CASES ARE MEANT TO GO RED LATER: 711 and 712 assert that ufs_root and ufs_mount still return ENOSYS, which is the cheapest possible reminder to move that boundary at 1.11a and 1.8b.  Mutation-verified four ways: a Reno-style minfree reserve (708), f_files without the i-list offset (709), a mount not forced read-only (703), and an unmount that leaves stale private data (715).  UFS 1.11c ADDED THE NAME LOOKUP, and cases 820-856 drive VOP_LOOKUP and VOP_READDIR directly with a nameidata built by hand rather than through namei -- driving the vnode op directly is what makes a failure name UFS rather than the walk above it.  The oracle is `fgxfs ls`, which reports the root of this volume as `.` and `..` at inode 2, `lost+found` at 3 and `big` at 4.  THE DIRECTORY FORMAT IS 2.11BSD's AND NOT RENO's: Reno opens `struct direct` with a 32-bit d_ino, so its header is eight bytes against 2.11BSD's six, and a port that took Reno's layout would read every name two bytes late.  Case 827 exists because it was BLOCKED: 1.11c landed with all of this uncalled on the reading that two consecutive lookups on the same directory hang inside Blk_Read, which was apple/fgx#183's wild return seen through a screen the machine had already erased.  Mutation-verified four ways, and the arms that did NOT go red are the informative ones.  RED: Reno's eight-byte directory header gives 821; readdir accepting an unaligned uio_offset gives 839; a dirmatch that compares d_namlen and never the name bytes gives 855; a lookup miss returning 0 instead of ENOENT gives 835.  NOT RED, and neither is a gap in the probe: stepping the scan by DIRSIZ instead of d_reclen is behaviourally IDENTICAL on a well-formed volume -- direnter makes every record exactly DIRSIZ except the last in a block, and a removed entry leaves a stale header the DIRSIZ walk follows just as far, so that rule is robustness against a CORRUPT directory and not a correctness property this volume can express; and returning the scan's result for `.` instead of the directory itself is identical too, because the scan finds inode 2, which is the directory, and the self-naming arm hands back the same vnode.  Case 855 was WRITTEN BECAUSE OF a mutation: the four names on this volume are 1, 2, 10 and 3 bytes long, all different, so before it every hit and every miss landed the same way whether or not the bytes were compared.  AND THE ORACLE JUDGES WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND.  `ufsfsck_check.py' fscks every staged spindle once the machine has finished with it, which is the campaign plan's phase-1 arm 1 -- "mount -t ufs survives a full read/write exercise; host fgxfs fsck clean".  It works even though this probe RESTORES the volume, because the restore is SEMANTIC rather than byte for byte: a completed run puts the free list and the counts back where it found them, so anything the exercise damaged OUTSIDE what it meant to touch still shows.  Measured on two completed runs: 305 used, 3,725 free, 1,020 free inodes, identical to a fresh mkfs.  IT IS NOT SELF-SUFFICIENT and must not be read as though it were -- a run that PANICS before doing anything leaves a clean volume too, which is exactly what apple/fgx#272 did -- so this arm is worth something only beside the `ufs: ok' above it and tryprobe.sh's exit status (apple/fgx#273). AND THE COMMAND ENDS IN `sync' FOR THE SAME REASON ITS THIRTEEN SIBLINGS DO, which is a property of the MACHINE and not of this probe: init creates /etc/utmp at every boot (init.c:640) and login(3) writes a record past its EOF, so the BOOT ITSELF takes a block off the free list and marks sb_fmod, and ufs_alloc writes the superblock back only when its batch of fifty empties. Nothing else calls sync(2) -- there is no update(8) here -- so a machine powered off at the prompt leaves the on-disk superblock still listing a block an inode owns. Measured with the probe OFF and the command `ls /': `block 14885 is on the FREE LIST and also owned by inode 499'; the same run as `ls /; sync' is clean. The claim this arm makes is therefore `consistent after a sync', which is what a filesystem promises; `consistent after a power cut' is fsck's job and is apple/fgx#330.

requires.reason: the filesystem probe is compiled into vfs.mod only at kernel.ufsprobe = 1, and it is a SEPARATE GATE from kernel.vfsprobe because the two do not fit in one 64 KB module bank -- see cfg/system.cfg.  It is off by default because it WRITES to a disk on the boot path.  Set kernel.ufsprobe = 1 in cfg/system.cfg, then run `python3 tools/ninja/gen.py` BEFORE ninja and re-run with --fresh.  The gen.py step is not optional and its absence does not look like an error: cfg/system.cfg feeds include/config.s through a generated edge, so editing the gate alone leaves ninja with nothing to do and the run silently tests the OLD setting.
